items.title: Georg Brunis Interview, 1958-06-03
items.q: Papa Lane used to pick me up, see? I played with his Reliance band, and he'd pick me up and we'd play the dance

ctx.x: So did you really play out there almost every night on the-

Well, no. When he felt in the mood, if he didn't eat too much, he'd say, all right, boys, get the instruments, and we'd have to be there. And I'll guarantee you, it's not like today. At nine o'clock, we hung out when we were playing music. Papa Lane used to pick me up, see? I played with his Reliance band, and he'd pick me up and we'd play the dance, and we'd get fifty cents an hour, Crescent Park, Owls Halls, Suburban Park, Elvira Park, and Algiers, and we'd play the parades. items.title: "Papa Jack" Laine, Mrs. "Papa Jack" Laine and Johnny Wiggs Interview, 1959-02-27
items.q: And Haley Brunus, and Georgie Brunus, and Merit Brunus, and Abby Brunus, and had Kaz Out. Oh, yeah, Jones Kaz Out. All them kids, you know, brothers, they played music. And I stood right between them and told them how to come down.

ctx.x: Jimmy Kennell. He played cornet too. He played with him too?

I was over, this was around about 1910. Somewhere along around 1910. I was in Biloxi. I had three bands in Biloxi. I had a junior band playing for the junior company. I had one for the West End and one for a volunteer. Three bands. Well, I had all kids. All youngsters ranged in Biloxi, I guess they'd say, from about 16 years down to eight. I had 14 pieces in that band. Mississippi Hook and Ladder was right across the park where we were in, what's the name, Kennedy's Hotel. The park was like here, Kennedy's Hotel…
They played all them halls, the Portuguese and the Washington of Terror, the out- I don't think- All that used to always have ordainances, you know, balls and all.

items.title: "Papa Jack" Laine Interview, 1964-04-25
items.q: And they seen all my kids, a bunch of my kids out. All little fellas. Like the Georgie Brunas, Henny Brunas, and all that bunch.

ctx.x: Yeah. You remember that one? That's old. Oh, yeah. Tell him I found a record of Kentucky Days yesterday. He found a record of Kentucky Days yesterday. Oh. Yeah.

That was my favorite. Is that right? I'll tell you a little instance that's happened about Kentucky Days. Now, this is a queer thing with our boy, Alfred. I've got three bands in Biloxi. Understand me? Uh-huh. I've got a band for West End Junior, band for West End Fire Company, number three, and a band for volunteer, number one. Okay. items.title: "Papa Jack" Laine Interview, 1957-03-26
items.q: Well, Brunus and all, they used to be with me all the time, the Brunus boys. The Brunus boys, especially Georgie Brunus, Georgie Brunus never left my home.

ctx.x: Was Vega a ragtime player or what did you

read on it? Oh, very good ragtime player. Very good. Very good. Yeah. In fact, as I'm telling you, well, him and Manuel Marlowe, in fact, were the first two kids that I picked up on horn. Then I began to get my boy, my boy, practicing and wanting it on this fellow, Mead and Perkins, pulled him through. And then got Johnny Lawler and boys like that in another place. Well, Brunus and all, they used to be with me all the time, the Brunus boys. The Brunus boys, especially Georgie Brunus, Georgie Brunus never left my…
Did they play regular cornets in those days or were they different?
